programme: No single module unifies these twelve factors. They fall into at least six unrelated regulatory families with non-overlapping target sets: FOS/JUND form the AP-1 dimer (targets like MMP1, EGFR, TP53, IL6 — stress/proliferation immediate-early response); NR5A2 and NR2F1 are nuclear receptors whose target lists (STAR, CYP11A1, HSD3B2, CYP17A1, CYP11B1) mark a steroidogenic/cholesterol-metabolism programme; GRHL3 runs an epithelial-barrier/differentiation set (CDH1, CLDN7, TFAP2A); XBP1 runs the unfolded-protein response (HSPA5, DNAJB9, DDIT3); ZBTB16 and CTCFL are hematopoietic/germline chromatin factors (KIT, CD34, CXCR4, MYC, BRCA1); TRPS1 is a chondrogenic repressor (RUNX2, SOX9); ID3 is a BMP/Notch differentiation-block factor; E2F7 is an atypical cell-cycle checkpoint repressor (E2F1/2, CDKN1A, VEGFA). None of these fragments shares targets or a documented physical/pathway relationship with another, so 'what these factors do together' has no honest single answer.
role_in_a: Not assignable as a module. In isolation, FOS has a documented role in HGF/MET-driven renal tubular mitogenesis, a pathway relevant to papillary RCC (MET-driven subtype), but this is a single-factor observation, not a shared programme with the rest of the list.
role_in_b: Not assignable as a module. In isolation, NR5A2 has a documented growth-promoting/chemoresistance role in glioma, but again this is one factor, not a module shared with the other eleven.
shared_axis: No mechanism in the record connects these factors as a group to both diseases; the only two on-topic papers each address a single factor in a single disease, and neither factor pair (FOS/JUND AP-1, or NR5A2/NR2F1 nuclear-receptor) has documented relevance to both a MET-driven renal epithelial tumor and an IDH-driven diffuse glioma.
reasoning: The concordance counts (135-178 of 434 comparisons) are moderate but the factors span at least six unrelated regulatory families with disjoint target sets, so no programme can be named that most of them carry together. Open Targets shows no disease association for nearly every factor in both diseases, and of the two papers that are on-topic, each supports only one factor in one disease alone — neither addresses the pair. Per the rule that a pair you cannot explain is a real result, this one should not be forced into a story.
support: PMID 36303447 — shows NR5A2 knockdown/miR-433-3p sensitizes glioma cells to cisplatin, i.e. NR5A2 is growth/resistance-promoting in glioma alone, not linked to any other listed factor or to kidney papillary cell carcinoma. PMID 9652757 — shows HGF stimulates c-fos induction during renal tubular mitogenesis, relevant background for MET-driven papillary RCC biology but not a papillary-RCC-specific study and not linked to glioma or to JUND/AP-1 as a complex. All other retrieved items are unjudgeable, off-topic (other cancers), or return no association for either disease.
how_to_falsify: Take the two candidate pairs that are at least biologically real complexes — FOS/JUND (AP-1) and NR5A2/NR2F1 (nuclear-receptor pair) — and test in matched patient-derived papillary RCC and LGG samples whether they co-occupy a shared target set (ChIP-seq/co-IP) and whether joint knockdown produces a convergent phenotype (proliferation, steroidogenic gene expression, or stress response) in both tumor types; if no shared occupancy or phenotype emerges in either pairing, the incoherent call stands. Finding a genuine shared target module and phenotype in both diseases would overturn this verdict.
caveats: Brain (glioma) vs kidney (RCC) is an anatomically and developmentally distant pairing; the 434 comparisons come from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the large comparison count reflects repeated clinical subgroupings within a limited number of underlying cohorts, not independent replication. The single-view exclusion list (PITX3, BCOR, HHEX, etc., each near-perfect in one group but recurrence 0.05-0.2 overall) shows this dataset readily produces cohort-specific spurious top hits, which argues for caution even with the concordant list. Tissue-generic immune/chromatin factors (STAT4, RFX5, EGR4, HDAC7, FOXP3) were already stripped before ranking, so the remaining heterogeneity is not an artifact of generic tissue regulators — the twelve factors are genuinely disparate in function.
